title: Escape on a Hint or field inside a Modal closes the whole dialog
body:
## Summary
Modal's document keydown listener closes on Escape unconditionally, so every child that 'stops' Escape (Hint popover, AssetLightbox's rename field) still closes the dialog.

## Description
Next 16 hydrates React on `document` itself (node_modules/next/dist/client/app-index.js:33 `const appElement = document`). React's delegated listener and Modal's own `document.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)` (components/ui/Modal.tsx:197) therefore sit on the SAME node. A synthetic `e.stopPropagation()` calls native stopPropagation, which stops propagation to the NEXT node but never to other listeners on the current one. So Hint.tsx:141-145 (`if (e.key === 'Escape' && open) { e.stopPropagation(); setOpen(false) }`) and app/library/AssetLightbox.tsx:350-353 (whose comment states the intent: 'Stopped here, or Modal reads it as close the dialog and the user loses the whole viewer') both fail: Modal.tsx:166-169 calls onCloseRef.current() regardless. 8 files put a Hint/Keycaps/StaleBadge inside a Modal or Sheet (e.g. app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx:261, app/library/AssetLightbox.tsx:128,197, app/foundry/Lightbox.tsx:176).

## Flow
- Open the project edit dialog, Tab to the lock Hint (ProjectDialog.tsx:261) - popover opens on focus.
- Press Escape to dismiss the popover.
- Hint closes AND Modal.tsx:166 fires on the same document node: the dialog closes, unsaved edits are dropped, focus returns to the opener.
- Same for AssetLightbox: Escape to abandon a rename closes the whole viewer.

## Expected impact
Escape regains its nesting: the innermost thing closes first. Removes a data-loss path (unsaved dialog edits) on every dialog that carries a disclosure.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - Escape inside a dialog dismisses the innermost open thing, not the dialog
Before: Node EventTarget probe (same-node semantics, v24.12.0): listener 1 = stopPropagation, listener 2 still fires with cancelBubble=true. Modal.tsx:166-169 has 0 guards on cancelBubble/defaultPrevented, so the 2 known stop sites (Hint.tsx:143, AssetLightbox.tsx:353) are 0/2 effective.
After: Modal's Escape branch returns early when `e.cancelBubble || e.defaultPrevented` - 2/2 stop sites effective; an un-stopped Escape still closes (unchanged).
Method: probe - node -e two listeners on one EventTarget (reproduced: second fires, cancelBubble=true) + next app-index.js:33 shows root === document
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/Modal.tsx:165-169,197; components/ui/signal/Hint.tsx:141-145; app/library/AssetLightbox.tsx:350-353; node_modules/next/dist/client/app-index.js:33 (appElement = document), :302 hydrateRoot(appElement); node probe output: 'Modal onKey fired; cancelBubble=true defaultPrevented=false'; 8 files with Hint/Keycaps/StaleBadge inside <Modal|<Sheet
verify: Write tests/golden-path/modal-escape-yields.probe.spec.ts first: (1) a Node EventTarget case pinning the premise (first listener stopPropagation -> second sees cancelBubble === true); (2) a source ratchet: stripComments(Modal.tsx) - inside the `e.key === "Escape"` branch, a `cancelBubble` (or `defaultPrevented`) early return appears before `onCloseRef.current()`. Red on HEAD (0 guards), green after. Then npm run typecheck (KeyboardEvent.cancelBubble is typed, deprecated-but-standard). Shares Modal.tsx with the actions-parity item: give both to one builder.

title: Four bell-tray controls delete themselves and drop focus on <body>
body:
## Summary
In the notification tray, 'mark all read', 'dismiss' (event), 'clear' (interrupted job) and 'dismiss' (storage trouble) each remove the very element that was clicked; focus falls to <body>.

## Description
The tray shows UNREAD events only (NotificationBell.tsx:3-7), so acting on a row removes it: markAllRead (l.282) unmounts its own button because it renders only while `count > 0` (l.278); markRead(act.eventId) (l.498) removes the <li>; clear(act.jobId) (l.408) removes the interrupted card; clearStorageTrouble (l.303) removes the trouble card. None hands focus anywhere. The same file already owns the destination: the panel is `tabIndex={-1}` with its own focus ring (l.262, l.272) and the open effect focuses it (l.168). Modal.tsx:54-64 states the cost of this exact shape in this repo ('From <body> the next Tab restarts at the top of the document').

## Flow
- Keyboard user opens the bell (focus moves into the tray, l.168).
- Tabs to 'dismiss' on an event and presses Enter.
- The <li> unmounts; document.activeElement === body; the tray is still open but the next Tab starts at the wordmark.

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can work down the tray one item at a time instead of re-entering it after every dismiss.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - after dismissing a notification, focus stays in the tray
Before: 4 self-unmounting handlers (NotificationBell.tsx:282, 303, 408, 498), 0 of 4 move focus.
After: 4 of 4 follow the state change with `panelRef.current?.focus()` (panel is already tabIndex=-1 and ringed).
Method: probe - source read: each handler's state change removes its own trigger (render conditions l.278, l.292, l.375, l.428/449)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:278-286 (count>0 gate + markAllRead), :301-307 (clearStorageTrouble), :402-412 (clear), :493-502 (markRead), :262/:272 (panel tabIndex=-1 + focus ring), :168 (panel focus on open); components/ui/Modal.tsx:54-64 (repo's own statement of the <body> cost)
verify: Write tests/golden-path/bell-focus-handoff.probe.spec.ts first: stripComments(NotificationBell.tsx); for each of the four calls markAllRead / clearStorageTrouble / clear(act.jobId) / markRead(act.eventId) used as an onClick, assert the same handler body also contains `panelRef.current?.focus()` (or one named helper that does). Count 0/4 on HEAD -> 4/4 after. Keep the existing bell-doors probe green.

title: Below 768px (or at 200% zoom) the Obsidian nav loses every module link
body:
## Summary
StudioFrame's module links sit in `hidden ... md:flex`, so under the md breakpoint Library, Board, Calendar, Sound lab and Foundry have no on-screen route at all.

## Description
components/ui/StudioFrame.tsx:177 `font-jetbrains hidden items-center gap-7 ... md:flex`. There is no menu, drawer or second row in its place - only the wordmark (-> /projects), the bell and the account control remain. The shell treats phones as real targets elsewhere (Modal.tsx:262 becomes a bottom sheet under `sm`; NotificationBell.tsx:263-271 sizes its tray for 360px Android), and the breakpoint is also crossed by desktop users zooming: a 1440px window at 200% is 720 CSS px, which fails WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (functionality lost, not reflowed). The Obsidian <nav> (l.164) also carries no accessible name while its Almanac twin is `aria-label="Places"` (components/kit/Bar.tsx:21).

## Flow
- Open /board (StudioFrame obsidian, app/board/page.tsx:17) at 390px wide, or at 200% zoom on a 1440px window.
- The module links are display:none; the only way to /library or /foundry is typing the URL.
- Screen readers hear an unnamed navigation landmark containing one link.

## Expected impact
Navigation survives narrow viewports and zoom; the five framed routes stop being URL-only below 768px.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every module is reachable at 390px and at 200% zoom
Before: Module links rendered below md: 0 of 6 (StudioFrame.tsx:177 `hidden`); obsidian <nav> accessible name: none.
After: 6 of 6 rendered below md (e.g. the same links as a full-width `scroll-x` second row: `order-last w-full md:order-none md:w-auto`); <nav aria-label="Places"> to match the Almanac Bar.
Method: probe - source read of the class list + Tailwind semantics (`hidden` = display:none until `md:flex`)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/StudioFrame.tsx:164 (<nav> unnamed), :177 (`hidden items-center gap-7 ... md:flex`); components/kit/Bar.tsx:21 (aria-label="Places"); components/ui/Modal.tsx:262 (sm: bottom sheet); components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:263-271 (360px target); StudioFrame obsidian consumers: app/board/page.tsx:17, app/calendar/page.tsx:18, app/foundry/FoundryView.tsx:396
verify: Write tests/golden-path/shell-nav-reflow.probe.spec.ts first: stripComments(StudioFrame.tsx); the element that maps MODULES in the obsidian branch must not carry a bare `hidden` class token, and the obsidian <nav> must carry an aria-label. Red on HEAD. Then photograph: CX_BASE=http://localhost:3007 node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs projects out.png --width 390 and --width 1920 - links visible at 390, desktop row unchanged at 1920.

title: Deck's 'why Next is disabled' line sits at 3.8:1; card footnote at 2.6:1
body:
## Summary
The text that explains a locked CTA, and the card footnote/eyebrow, are the faintest text in the deck - all under the 4.5:1 text floor on the #080a10 ink.

## Description
Deck.tsx:201 draws `blockedHint` - documented at l.53-56 as the thing that stops a disabled control being 'a wall, not a gate' - in `text-white/40` = 3.77:1. DeckCard.tsx:181 draws `footnote` in `text-white/30` = 2.59:1 on showcase and dense cards, while the SAME field on a hero card is `text-white/50` = 5.33:1 (DeckCard.tsx:307): one concept, two strengths. Eyebrows at DeckCard.tsx:321 and :400 are `text-white/35` = 3.14:1. Sibling primitives in this context already measured and fixed this exact problem: Field.tsx:24-27 (placeholder /25 -> /45 'measures 4.5:1') and Field.tsx:202-205 (unit /35 -> /50 'measures 5.2:1').

## Flow
- Create wizard, a 'control' stage not yet done: the reason Next is disabled renders at 3.77:1 beside the disabled button.
- Research/dense cards: the provenance footnote reads at 2.59:1, the eyebrow at 3.14:1.

## Expected impact
The one sentence a blocked user needs becomes legible; footnote reads the same on every card density.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the blocked-Next reason and card footnotes clear 4.5:1 on ink
Before: 4 text sites under 4.5:1 in Deck.tsx/DeckCard.tsx: /40 (3.77), /30 (2.59), /35 x2 (3.14) - computed WCAG ratio of white at that alpha over #080a10.
After: 0 sites: blockedHint /60 (7.30), footnote /50 (5.33, = hero), eyebrow /50 (5.33).
Method: probe - WCAG 2.x relative-luminance computation, white alpha-composited over INK #080a10 (tokens.ts:105)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/deck/Deck.tsx:53-57 (blockedHint contract), :201 text-white/40; components/ui/deck/DeckCard.tsx:181 text-white/30, :307 text-white/50 (hero footnote), :321 and :400 text-white/35; components/ui/Field.tsx:24-27, :202-205 (sibling measured fixes); ratios: a=.30->2.59, .35->3.14, .40->3.77, .45->4.50, .50->5.33, .60->7.30
verify: Write tests/golden-path/deck-text-contrast.probe.spec.ts first: stripComments of Deck.tsx and DeckCard.tsx; count `text-white/(30|35|40)\b` tokens -> 4 on HEAD, assert 0. Optionally compute the ratio from each `text-white/NN` on a text element with the WCAG formula and assert >= 4.5. npm run check:type stays green (no size change).

title: Modal's Obsidian branch silently drops `actions` (and `sheet`)
body:
## Summary
Modal documents `actions` as 'controls that sit beside the close button' and renders them only in the Almanac branch; the Obsidian branch never reads the prop.

## Description
Modal.tsx:117-119 declares `actions`; Modal.tsx:246 renders `{actions}` in the Almanac header; the Obsidian header (l.285-299) renders only the close button, and `variant` is likewise ignored there. This is not hypothetical scope: tokens.ts:262-267 declares WORLD_OBSIDIAN_KIT precisely so a route can render the kit's components - it names `Sheet` - in the Obsidian palette, and WorldRoot world="obsidian" (components/kit/WorldRoot.tsx:35) makes useWorld() return "obsidian", which CalendarView and AudioWorkbench already use. components/kit/Sheet.tsx:43 passes `actions` and `variant="sheet"`; in an obsidian-kit route its header actions would vanish without an error.

## Flow
- Render <Sheet actions={...}> under <WorldRoot world="obsidian"> (the supported combination per tokens.ts:265-266).
- Modal takes the Obsidian branch (Modal.tsx:261): no actions, panel width instead of a sheet.
- The caller's controls are simply absent.

## Expected impact
One dialog contract in both worlds; the kit's obsidian promise holds for Sheet.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a dialog's header actions render in either world
Before: `{actions}` rendered in 1 of 2 Modal branches; `sheet` honoured in 1 of 2. Live obsidian consumers today: 0 (Sheet's only caller is the almanac /kit specimen, app/kit/Parts.tsx:326) - latent, not yet hit.
After: `{actions}` rendered in 2 of 2 branches (beside the close button, Obsidian chrome).
Method: probe - source read; grep of `actions={` and `variant="sheet"` consumers
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: components/ui/Modal.tsx:117-119 (prop contract), :246 (almanac renders), :285-299 (obsidian header, no actions); components/kit/Sheet.tsx:43; components/ui/tokens.ts:262-267 (obsidian kit names Sheet); components/kit/WorldRoot.tsx:35; grep: Sheet consumers = app/kit/Parts.tsx:326 only
verify: Write tests/golden-path/modal-world-parity.probe.spec.ts first: stripComments(Modal.tsx) and count `{actions}` occurrences - 1 on HEAD, assert 2 (one per world branch). Shares Modal.tsx with the Escape item: one builder should take both.

Never-returns: AuthGate has no timeout, but onAuthStateChanged resolves from local persistence (lib/useAuth.ts:129) - not emitted.

Comment drift noted, not emitted (not rendered): NotificationBell.tsx:263-267 still says StudioFrame is `px-6`/`overflow-hidden` (now px-2 / overflow-clip, StudioFrame.tsx:142,163); tokens.ts:340-341 says --text-content 1rem / --text-label 0.875rem while globals.css:45-47 declares 1.125rem / 1rem.
